mostWorthwhile.text: Making winged insects was the most worthwhile step: flight gave them access to the canopy, and the explanation distinguished insect wings from vertebrate forelimbs.

leastWorthwhile.text: My two attempts to put animals directly into the forest were repetitive guesses; both needed compatibility feedback to redirect me.

surprise.text: The feedback turned my failed arthropod–forest pairing into insects with shore plants. The explanation clarified that plants provided habitat, not insect ancestry.

arbitrary.text: Combining insects with air to make wings felt like a symbolic shortcut rather than an explanation of how flight evolved, though the result acknowledged its distinct evolutionary history.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: adding insects made the forest feel more inhabited, and I would be curious to see how its relationships develop.
